new_integration_tests: drops the view and leaves the table and every row untouched

refuses to drop a table of the old name, and leaves its rows (asserted at the relation level, not only on the message)
refuses a materialized view under the old name

the relkind guard cases fail if the block drops without checking relkind, and the surviving rows prove the table was not touched

the registry tests in startup-migrations.test.ts failed on the un-updated expected list and the 140 ceiling until 0141 was added, which is the collision gate working

independent_review.reviewer: fresh read-only Claude context, not the author (founder review policy 2026-09-07)
fixed: the source_health guard checked presence, not relkind, so a hand-reversed rename could have orphaned the real table — now requires relkind r, with two new tests
the table-refusal test checked only the error message — now asserts the relation is still a table and still holds its row, plus a materialized-view case

the rollback hazard said 'older than 0134'; a build older than 0132 is already incompatible because 0132 dropped the SQS columns and sqs_daily_snapshot, which the view does not restore — reworded in the block header and the handoff
the production claim about once/retired blocks now says it comes from startup_migration_applied.last_applied_at, not from absent log lines
PROGRAM.md's Resume here still described H7 as active
left_as_is: the oldKind guard is partly redundant with Postgres refusing DROP VIEW on a table; kept for a readable operator message
a future block naming capability_health would pass on a fresh database and fail in production; the schema.ts comment warns against adding a reader
